Subject: Quick recap + vendor paperwork options (MediaCorp)

Hi Lauren —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same view: 

- Redwood contact: Soojin (Commercial) / Ben (Solutions) / Vanessa (CS)
- Goal: Get MediaCorp live on Redwood Hosted API for search & personalization pilot Q3
- Procurement path options discussed: PO (standard), corporate card (fastest), or marketplace (if you prefer consolidated billing)

Action items for MediaCorp:
1) Confirm preferred payment path (PO vs card vs marketplace) — this will determine paperwork.
2) If PO: please share AP contact and any vendor packet template.
3) If card: confirm cardholder/email to finish billing setup.
4) If marketplace: let us know which marketplace (AWS/Azure/GCP) and we’ll provide marketplace vendor IDs.

Attached: vendor_packet_v1.pdf (initial vendor packet — W-9 template, vendor form, high-level banking instructions). I can update for any specific fields you require.

Proposed Redwood next steps once you confirm path:
- If PO: we’ll send a completed vendor packet (W-9 + banking stub) and a DocuSign link for signature; ops typically needs ~5 business days to get vendor code set up after receiving full packet.
- If card: we’ll get billing set up and can start within 24–48 hours after card info is added.
- If marketplace: we’ll share marketplace listing and onboarding doc; timeline depends on marketplace enrollment approval.

Would you confirm which path MediaCorp prefers and the AP contact? Once we have that, Ben and I will follow up with the exact packet and timeline.

Thanks —
Sooj

--

Hi Soojin —

Appreciate the clear recap. Procurement here prefers to go the PO route for anything with vendor integrations. A few notes:

- AP contact for MediaCorp: Maria Gomez (maria.gomez@mediacorp.com)
- Standard terms: Net 30 preferred; we can discuss Net 45 if needed for initial pilot approvals
- We need the vendor packet (W-9 or W-8 if applicable), banking stub, and any completed vendor form compatible with our Ariba portal

Can you send a completed W-9 and the vendor packet back to me, and also include whether Redwood can accept the PO via email or if you need the PO through Ariba? We currently route most suppliers through Ariba for vendor creation but can accept email POs in limited cases.

Thanks —
Lauren

Thanks Lauren — that works.

I’ve attached an updated vendor packet (vendor_packet_v2.pdf) with a completed W-9 template (redwood_w9_template.pdf) and our vendor_onboarding_checklist.xlsx that outlines the fields we usually fill for Ariba. A few clarifications:

- Redwood can accept a PO via email to billing@redwood.ai OR via Ariba — whichever is preferred by your AP team.
- For Ariba: the fields in our checklist cover tax id, banking stub, remit address, and primary AP contact. If Maria needs a specific template, please forward and we’ll populate it exactly.
- DocuSign: I’ll send a DocuSign envelope for signature on the vendor packet to the primary signatory once you confirm the acceptance path. Link will be: https://docusign.com/envelopes/0a1b2c3d4e5f

Next steps on our side if PO is confirmed:
1) We finalize the packet and send DocuSign to the authorized signer.
2) Ops receives signed packet + banking stub and begins vendor setup (target 5 business days).
3) We issue invoice upon PO receipt and follow your Net 30 terms unless otherwise agreed.

If you’d like to evaluate the marketplace option as a fallback (sometimes procurement will prefer marketplace for consolidated billing), I can loop in our marketplace partner lead and share the marketplace vendor IDs — but that will add an extra enrollment step.

Attaching: vendor_packet_v2.pdf; redwood_w9_template.pdf; vendor_onboarding_checklist.xlsx

Best,
Sooj
